title: Apprentice Landing Checklist + Adaptive Interview Matrix (cohort pilot)
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a lightweight hiring and onboarding blueprint for an apprenticeship/cohort pilot focused on early-career platform engineers and SRE-facing infra apprentices. The design goal is: fast, low-friction assessment; bias-mitigated signals; and a 30->90 day staged autonomy path called the 'Skill Garden' (microtasks -> paired ownership -> independent ticketing).

Scope and constraints:
- Cohort size target: 6 apprentices per pilot (mix of engineering and infra ops).
- Budget: 6x junior salary + 2 mentors (0.2 FTE each) + tooling credits.
- Timeline: sourcing -> interview loop -> offer -> preboard -> day0 -> 30/60/90 follow-ups. Pilot runway: 12 weeks from posting to first cohort graduation.

Hiring plan (practical steps):
1) Sourcing & outreach (weeks -4 to -1):
   - Post compact role brief on site + diversity-focused channels.
   - 60% applicants from targeted community partners.
   - Screening: 10-question contextual form (experience, learning projects, access needs).
2) Screen -> Work sample (week -1):
   - 20 minute screening call focused on learning orientation and problem decomposition.
   - Send 48-hour micro-assignment (engineering notebook + 1 runnable script or architecture sketch).
3) Interview loop (week 0):
   - 60 min technical pairing (majority of time 1:1 pair-programming on a short infra task).
   - 45 min culture + team expectations conversation with mentor panel.
   - 30 min asynchronous practicum review (evaluate micro-assignment artifacts).
4) Making offers:
   - Scorecard uses 'adaptive rubric' (see matrix below).
   - Feedback consolidated in 48 hours; aim to extend offers within 72 hours of final interview.

Adaptive interview matrix (how to interpret signals):
Columns: Signal | Low | Medium | High | Evidence artifacts
- Problem decomposition | struggles to break problem into steps | can outline rough steps and trade-offs | precise steps, edge cases, alternatives | pairing transcript, micro-assignment notes
- Learning orientation | no examples of self-directed learning | has recent small-scale learning projects | continuous learning path, mentorship examples | screening answers, GitHub/Notion links
- System thinking (infra) | limited memory of systems | describes components but not failure modes | draws failure modes, recovery paths, telemetry needs | pairing session, sketch image
- Communication for handoffs | terse or unclear messages | mostly clear with follow-up questions | pro-active handoffs and docs | Slack snippets, doc drafts
- Bias-mitigation flag | over-index on pedigree, vague examples | concrete examples but limited context | specific, reproducible contributions | structured interview notes

Scoring mechanics (simple):
- Each signal graded 1/2/3 mapped to Low/Medium/High.
- Minimum pass: total >= 12 out of 18 with no critical 'Low' on learning orientation or communication for handoffs.
- Interviewer comments must include one concrete evidence item (link or snippet).

Onboarding: Preboard -> Day0 -> 30/60/90
Preboard (offer accepted -> day0):
- IT: laptop checklist and non-blocking access (email, dev VPN, ticketing read-only) delivered within 48 hours.
- Prework: short 'Skill Garden' primer (15–20 min reading/video) + first microtask repo stub.
- Buddy intro: assign mentor (buddy) and schedule day0 1:1.
Day0 (first day):
- Welcome call (30m) with people ops + hiring manager + mentor.
- Quick wins: run the repo tests, submit a doc PR, log a short intro in team channel.
- Safety: clarify psychological safety rituals and escalation path.
Days 1–14 (quiet launch window):
- Paired microtasks: apprentice pairs on 3 microtasks with mentors; daily 30m syncs.
- Weekly demo: 15m demo at weekly team sync.
Days 15–30 (gradual ownership):
- Shadowing lattice: apprentice observes 2 oncall rotations (read-only) and completes a small-ticket ownership (bugfix or infra alert triage runbook update).
- Autonomy checklist: can run deploy smoke-test flow and open a PR with basic testing.
30/60/90 milestones (assessment & calibration):
- 30d: mentor readiness check; update learning plan and microtask difficulty.
- 60d: independent ticket handling under review; initial hat of small subsystem.
- 90d: can lead a small improvement and present retrospective to mentor panel.

Mentor pairing and rotation protocol:
- Each apprentice has a primary mentor (0.2 FTE) and rotating secondary mentors (four 1-hour shadow sessions over first month).
- Mentor checklist: weekly learning outcome notes, pair log (short bullet list), one retrospective session at day 30.
- Escalation: mentor flags concerns early in an issues channel and books a calibration sync with people ops.

Evaluation rubric (sample items for 30/60/90):
- Technical craft: code quality, test coverage, ability to run infra flows.
- Operational readiness: follows runbook, understands failure signals.
- Communication: clear ticketing, docs, and async updates.
- Learning velocity: completes stretch microtasks with reduced scaffolding.
- Cultural fit: meets team norms for reliability and curiosity.
Each axis graded: red/orange/green; red requires action plan within 7 days.

Metrics to track for pilot success (signals, not perfect):
- Time-to-first-merge (median) per cohort
- Week-4 apprentice NPS (simple 7-point scale)
- Mentor FTE load % (goal <= 0.25 additional FTE per apprentice)
- Retention at 6 months (pilot follow-up)
- Hiring funnel velocity: days from app->offer

Risks & mitigation:
- Mentors overloaded: cap cohort size to mentor capacity; pre-agree on mentor time.
- Low signal from micro-assignment: provide more structured templates and scoring rubric.
- Accessibility needs: provide alternative non-coding assessment and extended deadlines.

Operational checklist (short TODOs):
- [ ] Finalize micro-assignment rubric and scoring sheet (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Create preboard Skill Garden primer + repo stub (owner: Jordan).
- [ ] Book mentor training slot (1 hour) on 'guided pairing' (owner: Maya).
- [ ] Prep offer letter addendum with cohort expectations (legal review).

Notes to reviewers / open questions:
- Should apprentices be placed in pods vs centralized cohort rotation? Pros/cons in comments.
- How strict should pass thresholds be for early cohorts — we recommend conservative acceptance for the first pilot to favor developmental investment.

Links / artifacts:
- Confluence: CONF-1221 (cohort-pilot-scope)
- Jira epic: PEOPLE-3120
- Micro-assignment template repo: github.com/redwood-inference/people-ops/apprentice-stubs

Appendix: Example micro-assignment (short)
- Objective: provision a small static site and add basic monitoring alert. Deliverables: 1) README with steps; 2) repo with infra-as-code snippet (3–10 lines) or dockerfile; 3) 1 paragraph retrospective with what they learned. Deadline: 48 hours.

Voice: This doc is a working draft; comments inline welcomed. Plan to iterate after first cohort debrief.
